summary: SQLite trim removes characters from both ends of text.
documentation: SQLite trim removes characters from both ends of text. The optional second argument is a set of removable characters, not a prefix or suffix substring. Interior characters remain unchanged.
returns: Text with matching edge characters removed, or NULL.
caution: With one argument, SQLite trims ordinary spaces, not every Unicode whitespace character. Tabs are not removed by that default.
scenarios: Remove edge padding from imported product labels.
Clean padded ASCII search terms inside a report.
Normalize a known delimiter-padding convention without touching interior spaces.
title: Remove ordinary edge spaces
problem: From labels(id INTEGER, name TEXT), return id and trim(name) as cleaned, ordered by id. Remove ordinary spaces at both edges only; preserve interior spaces and tabs. NULL remains NULL.
goal: Use trim() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use the one-argument SQLite trim behavior.
